reuse.why: Reuses findOrCreateBank, syncAccount, handleSyncResponse and extracts clearAccountLink so unlinkAccount and the takeover share it, but the Fintegra linker and downloader are written by copying the Akahu ones instead of sharing them.

duplication.why: linkFintegraAccount is a near line-for-line copy of linkAkahuAccount (~70 lines) and downloadFintegraTransactions a copy of downloadAkahuTransactions (~35 lines); the link rules themselves are centralised in one helper.

placement.why: Link rules live in a helper in accounts/app.ts next to the linkers, the download in sync.ts, the URL in server-config and the type in types/models, matching the tree's layering; the helper named assert* also performs the unlink side effect.

scope.why: Changes are what the four steps require (plus the client Record entries forced by SYNC_PROVIDERS); the DbAccount union edit adding only 'fintegra' is a small incidental change.

maintainability.why: One shared guard called by every linker is easy to own, but a sixth copy-pasted linker and downloader means future link changes must be made in yet another copy, and the assert helper mutating another account is surprising.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All six link handlers call assertBankAccountCanBeLinked; unlinkAccount now uses clearAccountLink; processBankSyncDownload reuses the akahu balance branch for fintegra.

disguised_duplication.where: The duplication (linkFintegraAccount vs linkAkahuAccount in accounts/app.ts, downloadFintegraTransactions vs downloadAkahuTransactions in sync.ts) is plain copy, not reshaped or renamed to hide it.

abstraction_drift.where: assertBankAccountCanBeLinked gains replaceExistingLink in step 4 (a real rule from the request) and the closed-account check applies to every provider; no provider-specific branches inside it and every linker, including the new Fintegra one, calls it.
